title: Jay Puri Among Names Reported in Nvidia Succession Talk as Board Backs Huang
excerpt: Nvidia has named no successor to Jensen Huang and its board says it backs him during an independent investigation, but AP reporting cited by Inshorts lists former worldwide sales chief Jay Puri, CFO Colette Kress, chief scientist Bill Dally and co-founder Chris Malachowsky among possible frontrunners if the board ever acts.
body:
• Nvidia has no publicly named successor to CEO Jensen Huang, and its board said on November 8 that it has confidence in him during an independent investigation.
  • AP reporting cited by Inshorts lists Indian-origin executive Jay Puri among possible frontrunners, alongside CFO Colette Kress, chief scientist Bill Dally and co-founder Chris Malachowsky.
  • Puri joined Nvidia in 2005 after 22 years at Sun Microsystems and ran worldwide field operations, the company's global sales and customer relationships.
  • Reports differ on Puri's current status: Inc. reported he retired from Nvidia in July 2026 after more than 20 years at the company.

Nvidia, valued at about $4.5 trillion, has never named a successor to Jensen Huang, the co-founder who has run the company since 1993. That gap has become a live question this week because Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation connected to reporting about Huang, while stating that it backs him and that he remains chief executive.

According to Inshorts, summarising Associated Press reporting, the frontrunners to replace Huang if the board decided to remove him could include Indian-origin executive Jay Puri and CFO Colette Kress, with chief scientist Bill Dally and co-founder Chris Malachowsky also named. No appointment has been made, and Nvidia has announced no shortlist.

Who Jay Puri Is

Ajay "Jay" Puri joined Nvidia in 2005 after a 22-year career at Sun Microsystems, and had earlier worked at HP and Texas Instruments, according to Inshorts. At Nvidia he oversaw worldwide field operations — sales, business development and programme management — and the customer relationships with the company's biggest buyers, according to Nvidia's annual report, which listed him among the executive officers below Huang.

That customer network is the case for Puri in succession speculation: the executive who ran global sales knows the hyperscalers and governments whose orders drive Nvidia's revenue. There is a complication, reported by Inc.: Puri retired from Nvidia in July 2026 after more than 20 years, which could complicate any return to lead the company. Inc.'s list of six possible successors also included Huang's children Madison Huang and Spencer Huang, who hold roles at the company.

A Board Investigation, and a CEO Staying in Place

On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia's board said it was opening an independent investigation "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The board said it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised, that Huang fully supports the review, and that it has confidence in him and his leadership team. Huang, 63, is described in the board's statement as committed to continuing to lead Nvidia without interruption.

The board has set no timetable for the review and has not said what it will do with the findings.

Why There Is No Obvious Heir

Bloomberg reported in January that Nvidia lacks a clear successor to Huang, and The New York Times has reported the company does not appear to have a succession plan or an obvious internal candidate, with around 60 senior executives reporting directly to Huang. Huang himself said on the Lex Fridman Podcast in March that he does not believe in succession planning.

For now, the succession question is hypothetical. Huang remains CEO, the board publicly supports him, and the names in circulation — Puri included — come from reporting about who the board could turn to, not from any Nvidia announcement. What the episode has established is narrower: the world's most valuable chip company has no public answer to who runs it if its founder cannot.
